attributes.body_ja:
「癖（くせ）」は「習慣（しゅうかん）になった行動（こうどう）」や「その人（ひと）の傾向（けいこう）」を表（あらわ）す名詞（めいし）です。たいていは悪（わる）いことについて使（つか）われます。「くせに」は、この名詞（めいし）「癖（くせ）」に格助詞（かくじょし）「に」が合（あ）わさってできています。この表現（ひょうげん）は「(A) なのに」という意味（いみ）で、主（おも）に (A) という状態（じょうたい）なのに (B) をする相手（あいて）の行動（こうどう）を責（せ）めたり、バカにしたりするような場面（ばめん）で使（つか）われます。

「くせ」は名詞（めいし）なので、「くせに」は連体形（れんたいけい）の語（ご）のあとに付（つ）きます。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「癖（くせ）」はもともと「その人（ひと）の（好（この）みなどによる）傾向（けいこう）」を表（あらわ）す言葉（ことば）で、悪（わる）い意味（いみ）で使（つか）われていたわけではありませんでした。しかし、これに「に」がつくことで、「本来（ほんらい）なら (A) になるはずなのに、(B) の行動（こうどう）がそれに合（あ）っていない」という不満（ふまん）を表（あらわ）すようになりました。
attributes.body:
癖（くせ） is a noun that means 'habit' or 'tendency'. However, as it usually refers to a negative thing, 'vice' is another accurate translation. くせに (usually appearing without kanji) is the combination of くせ, and the case marking particle に. This structure is often used to criticize the actions of others, and is used in a similar way to 'despite', 'even though', or 'and yet' in English.

As くせ is a noun, くせに may be used after the attributive form of any other word.

Fun Fact

癖（くせ） is a word that has developed a 'negative' meaning over time. Originally, 癖（くせ） was used to convey a preference, or the side that someone or something tended to lean toward (due to it being favorable for some reason). When adding the case marking particle に to this, it merely expressed that (A) was the preferable state/location, so (B) not being/not acting in a way appropriate for (A) is less than desirable.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.body: Both くせに and にもかかわらず convey contradiction between two facts, but with different nuance and tone. くせに is a casual expression with a blaming or critical tone, e.g. 知っているくせに何で教えてくれないの？ ('You know, so why won't you tell me!?'). In contrast, にもかかわらず is a more neutral and formal way to say 'in spite of (A)', e.g. 雨にもかかわらず出かけた ('We went out despite the rain.').

second_relatable.title: にもかかわらず
second_relatable.meaning: Despite, In spite of, Regardless, Nevertheless

attributes.body: Both くせに and つつ(も) express contradiction, but differ in tone. くせに is a casual expression with a blaming or critical tone, e.g. 知っているくせに何で教えてくれないの？ ('You know, so why won't you tell me!?'). つつ(も) is neutral and used to describe conflicting simultaneous actions, e.g. 危険だと知りつつも行った ('I went despite knowing at the same time that it was dangerous.').

second_relatable.title: つつ(も)
second_relatable.meaning: Even while ~ing, Even though ~ing, Despite ~ing, Although ~ing

attributes.body: Both のに and くせに express contrast, but with different nuance. のに is relatively neutral, like 'although', while くせに adds a strong negative or critical tone. For example, 頭がいいのにやる気がない and 頭がいいくせにやる気がない both mean 'Although (he's) smart, (he) has no motivation.', the のに version is just stating a fact, while the くせに version implies that his lack of motivation is a negative trait and not befitting of him.

くせに expresses disapproval, similar to 'in spite of' or 'although' in English. In contrast, が is a neutral connecting particle, often expressing contrast (like 'but') or adding information (like 'and'). Unlike くせに, which carries a negative nuance, が is neutral. After な-Adjectives and nouns, くせに requires な or の, while が requires だ or です.

ながらも and くせに both express contradiction, but differ in nuance. ながらも simply expresses two seemingly contradictory states coexisting in a neutral fashion, e.g. 緊張しながらもわくわくしている ('While feeling anxious, I'm also excited.'). In contrast, くせに implies blame or criticism, e.g. 知っているくせに教えてくれない ('Even though he knows, he won't tell me.').

first_relatable.title: ながらも
first_relatable.meaning: But, Even while, Even though, Despite, Although

attributes.body: Both express contrast, but differ in usage and implication. くせに follows a phrase and has a critical tone, e.g. 知っているくせに教えてくれない ('He knows but won't tell me.'), implying that the speaker is angry at the person. それなのに comes at the beginning of a sentence, is neutral, and expresses simple contradiction, e.g. 彼は真実を知っている。それなのに、教えてくれない ('He knows. And yet, he won't tell me.') with an objective nuance.

それでも and くせに both express contrast, but differ in tone. それでも is neutral, like the English 'even so'. くせに adds a critical nuance, often pointing out something negative or unjustified, e.g. 若いくせにやる気がない ('Even though he's young, he has no motivation.'), which implies disapproval.

first_relatable.title: それでも
first_relatable.meaning: But still, And yet, Even so, Nevertheless
